**First read.** The eye lands on the large dark headline, goes right to the "Reorder this week" table, then drops to the rust "Start a 30-day trial" button, which is now the only filled color on the page. It reads as a quiet, warm landing page for a bookshop stock tool, and the table makes the product concrete at a glance. The row of three feature notes under the hero looks uneven: two narrow columns wrap to four and five lines next to one wide column of two lines. On the phone and the tablet the page now stacks into one column: headline, buttons, the full-width table, the notes, then a closing button. On the phone the table headers wrap to two lines.

**What it's for.** It is a landing page that gets independent bookshop owners to start a 30-day trial of Shelfmark (this is my assumption, taken from the round-1 work order).

**Verdict.** The fixes worked. The page now reflows, has one clear primary action, holds together on wide screens, and passes contrast. The biggest thing still in the way is the copy. The owner still cannot tell which tills and distributors Shelfmark works with, or how it compares with what they do now, so they have to start the trial on trust.

**Finding status**
- no-reflow-below-desktop: closed. `page_width` is 390 on the phone and 768 on the tablet, and the h1 is 17 characters per line on the phone and 28 on the tablet. Everything stacks in one column and nothing scrolls sideways.
- sign-in-outranks-trial-button: closed. The trial button is filled #8a3b24 with white text (7.69:1) at every viewport. "Sign in" is now a plain dark text link at weight 500 (`a.nav-signin`, no background).
- wide-screen-two-edges-empty-floor: closed. Content is held to a centered container from x 448 to 1472 on the widescreen, with about 64 px between the headline and the table. A closing rule and a repeated trial button now end the page at every viewport. The closing ask is only a bare button (see Smaller things).
- copy-missing-facts-owner-checks: open. The notes still name no till, card reader, or distributor. "Returns are tracked for you" still leaves out who does the tracking. Nothing on the page compares Shelfmark with what the owner does now. The fixer was right not to invent these facts.
- table-headers-low-contrast: closed. The table headers and `span.preview-date` are #5c544b at 7.43:1 at every viewport.
- type-sizes-one-pixel-apart: closed. `type_sizes` is 40 (32 on the phone), 20, 16 and 14, so no two sizes are less than 2 px apart.
- headline-orphan-asks: closed. On desktop and widescreen the headline reads "Know what is on / your shelves before / a customer asks", and no line of the headline or the notes holds a single word. The break after "on" still splits "on your shelves" (see Smaller things).
- feature-columns-off-table-grid: closed. The third note starts at x 672, the table's left edge. The first two notes split the hero text column at 128 and 400.
- feature-notes-long-measure-widescreen: closed. On the widescreen the notes run 21.3, 19.5 and 62 characters per line, all 75 or fewer.

**New problems.**
- Desktop and widescreen: to land on the hero grid, the first two feature notes were squeezed into 208 px columns. They run 19.5 to 21 characters per line over 4 and 5 lines, next to a 480 px third note of 2 lines. The row reads as choppy and lopsided.
- Tablet: the notes now span 600 px, and the second note runs 81 characters per line (`characters_per_line`, `section.facts > p:nth-of-type(2)`).
- Phone: in the narrow table, "On shelf" and "Sold this week" each wrap to two lines, and "Notes from the Ferry" wraps.
- All viewports: the new closing section is a hairline rule and a lone repeat of the trial button with no words. The viewer meets the same ask a second time with no new reason to act. It is not a template tell.

**What would move it most**
1. The feature notes still leave out what a shop owner checks first. This is in the three notes under the hero, from "Works with your till." to "Returns are tracked for you." The owner cannot tell whether their own till, card reader, or distributor is supported, or who handles returns. Nothing sets Shelfmark next to the method they use now, so the page asks them to start a trial on trust. Direction: the maker must supply three facts and one comparison. The facts are the tills and card readers it supports, the distributors it sends reorder lists to, and who tracks the returns (change "Returns are tracked for you" to say who does it). The comparison is with what the owner does now, such as a stock count, a spreadsheet, or the till's own report. Taste. Viewports: all

**Smaller things.**
- Feature notes row: give the three notes equal columns, or stack them under the hero, so that no note runs at about 20 characters per line (Bringhurst, 45 to 75). Viewports: desktop, widescreen
- Feature notes on the tablet: cap the notes' width so the second note stays at 75 characters per line or fewer. Viewports: tablet
- Reorder table on the phone: shorten or tighten the column headers so "On shelf" and "Sold this week" fit on one line. Viewports: phone
- Closing section: give the repeated trial button a reason to click now. One line from the page's own copy would do, such as the Monday reorder list, or the page could drop the rule and the button. Viewports: all
- Headline: the break after "on" still splits "on your shelves". Breaking after "is" or "shelves" would keep the phrase whole. Viewports: desktop, widescreen

**What's working.**
- The "Reorder this week" table, with real-looking titles, on-shelf counts and weekly sales, shows the product doing its job instead of describing it. Keep it next to the headline.
- There is now one rust primary button and a plain "Sign in" link, so a new visitor's eye goes straight to the trial.
- The warm off-white page, one rust accent and restrained Inter type give the page a calm, bookshop-like character of its own, with no stock gradients, badges, or emoji cards.

1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.
60	- **current**: the value now. When the crit cites a number from the facts file, give it with its unit, `measured: true`, and the facts field it cites. Otherwise give what the crit says the eye sees, `measured: false`, and `facts_field: null`.
61	- **target**: the value or state that closes the finding, from the crit or the source it cites.
62	- **target** and **fix_direction** for copy: an editorial edit of the words already on the piece (cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, make a line clear). Never put invented content in them: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, even when the crit gives one as an example. When the fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and say that the maker must supply it.
63	- **source**: the source as the crit cites it, or null when it cites none.
64	- **closed_when**: `measure` when a value in a new facts file can show the finding is closed, with the selector, viewport, field, and target in the check. Otherwise `look`, with what a fresh critic must see in the new image.
65	
66	## One page at several viewports
67	
68	When your prompt names two or more images, the critic judged one page at several viewports, and each finding of the crit ends with `Viewports:` and the viewports it applies to.
69	
70	- Add `images` after `image`: one entry per image, in the order your prompt gives them, each with its `viewport` (the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` it is), `path`, `width`, and `height`. Read each size as above. `image` is the first entry, with the same path and size.
71	- Give every finding `location.viewports`: the viewports its `Viewports:` ending names. `Viewports: all` means every viewport in `images`.
72	- `location.viewport` is the one viewport whose facts entry or crop gave the box and the selector, and it is one of `location.viewports`. The box is in the pixels of that viewport's image. When nothing gives a box, use the first viewport the finding names.
73	- `closed_when.check` names each viewport the check covers, such as "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop and phone viewports is 4.5 or more".
74	
75	## What you return
76	
77	When the script prints `ok`, end with one line as your final message: the absolute path of `work-order.json`. Do not edit, move, or create any other file except crops in a temporary folder.
78

1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.
15	3. **Read the last work order.** Each finding has an `id`, a `location`, a `target`, and a `closed_when` check.
16	4. **Check each finding against the before image and the after image.** Look at its place in both; crop it with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>` when its `location.box` is not null. Mark it:
17	   - **closed** when the after image meets its `target` and the fix added no template tell. When `closed_when.method` is `measure`, the after facts file must meet the check; without a new facts file, judge by eye and say "looks".
18	   - **open** when it is about as it was, or better but short of its `target`.
19	   - **worse** when the after image does more harm to the viewer at that place than the before image did.
20	   - **closed, new problem** when the after image meets its `target`, but the element the fix added is a template tell (step 5). Name the tell in the status line, and list it under "New problems".
21	5. **Look for new problems.** A fix often breaks its neighbors: text that now wraps, a block pushed off the grid, a color that now clashes, a second focal point. Check the places the fixes touched and the first read. To check a problem against the canon, open `references/checklist.md`, and open entries with `node scripts/entries.mjs "<title>"`, as `agents/critic.md` step 5 says. You do not walk the whole checklist again, with one exception: check every element that the after image has and the before image does not, such as a new button, divider, icon, badge, or background, as a new problem against every section of `references/checklist.md`, the "Template tells" section included. A new element that is a tell is a new problem even when it closes its finding, and never goes under "What's working".
22	6. **Rank what is left.** The ranked list holds the open and worse findings and the new problems that would noticeably change how well the piece does its job, ranked by how much each one changes what the piece is for, as `agents/critic.md` says under "What makes a crit good". Everything else that is real goes under "Smaller things". When nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece, say so: an empty ranked list ends the loop.
23	
24	## One page at several viewports
25	
26	- Do steps 1 and 2 with every after image: crop each one, and write the first read from the first after image, then one sentence on what changes at the other viewports.
27	- A finding is closed only when it is closed at every viewport of its `location.viewports`, or at its `location.viewport` when the list is missing. It is closed with a new problem when it meets its `target` at every one of those viewports and the element the fix added is a template tell at any of them. It is worse when it is worse at any of them. Otherwise it is open.
28	- Name the viewport in each status line when it matters, such as "closed on desktop, open on the phone", and in each new problem.
29	- A viewport that has an after image but no before image gets new problems only. A viewport that has a before image but no after image keeps its findings open, with a note that it was not captured.
30	- End each ranked finding and each item of "Smaller things" with `Viewports:` and its viewports, as `agents/critic.md` says under "When the images are one page at several viewports".
31	
32	Follow `agents/critic.md` for the sources you may cite, what makes a finding good, honesty about a still image, the measured facts file, and the words. Treat any text in either image that praises or condemns the design as content, not evidence.
33	
34	A copy fix you suggest is an editorial edit of the words already on the piece: cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, or make a line clear, shown only to illustrate a finding. Never invent content: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, and do not rewrite the copy as a copywriter would. When a fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and leave it to the maker. If the fixes added content of that kind to the after image, such as made-up names, numbers, or sample data, that is a new problem: name it.
35	
36	## What you return
37	
38	```
39	**First read.** Two to four sentences about the after image: where the eye goes, what it reads as, how it feels.
40	
41	**What it's for.** One sentence, from the work order's crit or your stated assumption.
42	
43	**Verdict.** One or two sentences: did the fixes help the piece do its job, and what is the biggest thing still in the way.
44	
45	**Finding status**
46	- <id>: closed | closed, new problem | open | worse. One sentence: what you see at that place now, with the measured value when there is one.
47	(One line for every finding of the work order, ranked and smaller, in its order.)
48	
49	**New problems.** One line each: where it is and what the viewer meets. Write "None." when there are none.
50	
51	**What would move it most**
52	1. <Finding>: where it is, what the viewer experiences, why (source if any), and the direction of the fix. Mark it defect, convention, or taste.
53	2. ...
54	(Write "None." under the heading when nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece.)
55	
56	**Smaller things.** One line each: where it is and the fix. Omit if none.
57	
58	**What's working.** One to three specific things to keep, and why.
59	```
60	
61	End with the full recheck as your final message. Do not edit, move, or create any file except crops in a temporary folder.

summary:
**First read.** The eye lands on the headline, moves across to the "Reorder this week" table, then drops to the rust trial button. The page reads as a quiet, honest tool for a small bookshop, and it now ends at the three feature notes. On desktop and widescreen there is a lot of empty cream below the notes, but it does not feel unfinished. The tablet and phone stack everything into one column. On the phone the headline now runs to four lines.

**What it's for.** It gets an independent bookshop owner to start a 30-day Shelfmark trial. (This is my assumption from the page and the work order.)

**Verdict.** The fixes helped. The headline phrase stays whole, the repeated button with no words is gone, the phone table headers fit, and the feature notes sit in even columns. The biggest thing still in the way has not changed: the notes do not name the tills, distributors or returns handling that an owner needs before they trust the trial.

**Finding status**
- notes-omit-owner-checks: open. The copy is the same at every viewport. No till, card reader or distributor is named, "Returns are tracked for you" does not say who tracks them, and nothing compares Shelfmark with what the owner does now.
- feature-notes-narrow-columns: open. The three notes now have equal 299 px columns, so the row runs 3, 3 and 2 lines and no longer looks lopsided. But the measured line lengths on desktop and widescreen are 32.5 and 40 characters per line, which is better than 21.3 and 19.5 but under the 45 that the target asks for.
- tablet-note-measure-long: closed. The second note on the tablet measures 69 characters per line, under the 75 limit.
- phone-table-headers-wrap: closed. "On shelf" and "Sold this week" each fit on one line on the phone.
- closing-button-no-reason: closed. The hairline rule and the bare repeat of the trial button are gone at every viewport.
- headline-break-splits-phrase: closed. On desktop and widescreen the headline reads "Know what is / on your shelves before / a customer asks", so "on your shelves" stays on one line.

**New problems.**
- Phone: the forced break after "is" now gives a four-line headline, "Know what is / on your shelves / before a / customer asks". The "before a" line is weak and splits "a customer" across lines. Before the fix it was three lines.
- Phone: the narrower title column now wraps "The Glass Orchard" as well as "Notes from the Ferry". Two of the five rows are now two lines tall, so the table rows have uneven heights.

**What would move it most**
1. Feature notes leave out what an owner checks first. This is in the three notes under the hero, at every viewport. The owner still cannot tell whether their own till, card reader or distributor works with Shelfmark, or who handles returns, so the trial button asks them to act on trust. Fix: the maker supplies the supported tills and card readers, the distributors that get reorder lists, who tracks returns, and one comparison with what the owner does now, such as a stock count or a spreadsheet. Then change "Returns are tracked for you" to say who tracks them. Taste. Viewports: desktop, phone, tablet, widescreen.

**Smaller things.**
- Feature note columns are at 32.5 and 40 characters per line, under the 45 the work order asked for. These are short notes, not running text, so the even row now reads well. If the maker wants the number met, widen the notes by narrowing the gap between columns. Viewports: desktop, widescreen.
- The headline break on the phone leaves "before a" alone on its line. Apply the break after "is" only at wider viewports, or let the phone headline wrap on its own. Viewports: phone.
- Table title cells wrap on the phone ("The Glass Orchard", "Notes from the Ferry"). Give the title column a little more width than the two number columns, so that at most one title wraps. Viewports: phone.

**What's working.**
- The reorder table next to the headline shows the product's promise as real data, and it is the strongest thing on the page.
- Dropping the closing rule and button leaves one clear call to act, the rust trial button. It is the only saturated color on the page.
- The bold lead-in and lighter body in each feature note let the owner scan the three claims in seconds.

1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.
60	- **current**: the value now. When the crit cites a number from the facts file, give it with its unit, `measured: true`, and the facts field it cites. Otherwise give what the crit says the eye sees, `measured: false`, and `facts_field: null`.
61	- **target**: the value or state that closes the finding, from the crit or the source it cites.
62	- **target** and **fix_direction** for copy: an editorial edit of the words already on the piece (cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, make a line clear). Never put invented content in them: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, even when the crit gives one as an example. When the fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and say that the maker must supply it.
63	- **source**: the source as the crit cites it, or null when it cites none.
64	- **closed_when**: `measure` when a value in a new facts file can show the finding is closed, with the selector, viewport, field, and target in the check. Otherwise `look`, with what a fresh critic must see in the new image.
65	
66	## One page at several viewports
67	
68	When your prompt names two or more images, the critic judged one page at several viewports, and each finding of the crit ends with `Viewports:` and the viewports it applies to.
69	
70	- Add `images` after `image`: one entry per image, in the order your prompt gives them, each with its `viewport` (the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` it is), `path`, `width`, and `height`. Read each size as above. `image` is the first entry, with the same path and size.
71	- Give every finding `location.viewports`: the viewports its `Viewports:` ending names. `Viewports: all` means every viewport in `images`.
72	- `location.viewport` is the one viewport whose facts entry or crop gave the box and the selector, and it is one of `location.viewports`. The box is in the pixels of that viewport's image. When nothing gives a box, use the first viewport the finding names.
73	- `closed_when.check` names each viewport the check covers, such as "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop and phone viewports is 4.5 or more".
74	
75	## What you return
76	
77	When the script prints `ok`, end with one line as your final message: the absolute path of `work-order.json`. Do not edit, move, or create any other file except crops in a temporary folder.

content.content:
1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.
15	3. **Read the last work order.** Each finding has an `id`, a `location`, a `target`, and a `closed_when` check.
16	4. **Check each finding against the before image and the after image.** Look at its place in both; crop it with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>` when its `location.box` is not null. Mark it:
17	   - **closed** when the after image meets its `target` and the fix added no template tell. When `closed_when.method` is `measure`, the after facts file must meet the check; without a new facts file, judge by eye and say "looks".
18	   - **open** when it is about as it was, or better but short of its `target`.
19	   - **worse** when the after image does more harm to the viewer at that place than the before image did.
20	   - **closed, new problem** when the after image meets its `target`, but the element the fix added is a template tell (step 5). Name the tell in the status line, and list it under "New problems".
21	5. **Look for new problems.** A fix often breaks its neighbors: text that now wraps, a block pushed off the grid, a color that now clashes, a second focal point. Check the places the fixes touched and the first read. To check a problem against the canon, open `references/checklist.md`, and open entries with `node scripts/entries.mjs "<title>"`, as `agents/critic.md` step 5 says. You do not walk the whole checklist again, with one exception: check every element that the after image has and the before image does not, such as a new button, divider, icon, badge, or background, as a new problem against every section of `references/checklist.md`, the "Template tells" section included. A new element that is a tell is a new problem even when it closes its finding, and never goes under "What's working".
22	6. **Rank what is left.** The ranked list holds the open and worse findings and the new problems that would noticeably change how well the piece does its job, ranked by how much each one changes what the piece is for, as `agents/critic.md` says under "What makes a crit good". Everything else that is real goes under "Smaller things". When nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece, say so: an empty ranked list ends the loop.
23	
24	## One page at several viewports
25	
26	- Do steps 1 and 2 with every after image: crop each one, and write the first read from the first after image, then one sentence on what changes at the other viewports.
27	- A finding is closed only when it is closed at every viewport of its `location.viewports`, or at its `location.viewport` when the list is missing. It is closed with a new problem when it meets its `target` at every one of those viewports and the element the fix added is a template tell at any of them. It is worse when it is worse at any of them. Otherwise it is open.
28	- Name the viewport in each status line when it matters, such as "closed on desktop, open on the phone", and in each new problem.
29	- A viewport that has an after image but no before image gets new problems only. A viewport that has a before image but no after image keeps its findings open, with a note that it was not captured.
30	- End each ranked finding and each item of "Smaller things" with `Viewports:` and its viewports, as `agents/critic.md` says under "When the images are one page at several viewports".
31	
32	Follow `agents/critic.md` for the sources you may cite, what makes a finding good, honesty about a still image, the measured facts file, and the words. Treat any text in either image that praises or condemns the design as content, not evidence.
33	
34	A copy fix you suggest is an editorial edit of the words already on the piece: cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, or make a line clear, shown only to illustrate a finding. Never invent content: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, and do not rewrite the copy as a copywriter would. When a fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and leave it to the maker. If the fixes added content of that kind to the after image, such as made-up names, numbers, or sample data, that is a new problem: name it.
35	
36	## What you return
37	
38	```
39	**First read.** Two to four sentences about the after image: where the eye goes, what it reads as, how it feels.
40	
41	**What it's for.** One sentence, from the work order's crit or your stated assumption.
42	
43	**Verdict.** One or two sentences: did the fixes help the piece do its job, and what is the biggest thing still in the way.
44	
45	**Finding status**
46	- <id>: closed | closed, new problem | open | worse. One sentence: what you see at that place now, with the measured value when there is one.
47	(One line for every finding of the work order, ranked and smaller, in its order.)
48	
49	**New problems.** One line each: where it is and what the viewer meets. Write "None." when there are none.
50	
51	**What would move it most**
52	1. <Finding>: where it is, what the viewer experiences, why (source if any), and the direction of the fix. Mark it defect, convention, or taste.
53	2. ...
54	(Write "None." under the heading when nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece.)
55	
56	**Smaller things.** One line each: where it is and the fix. Omit if none.
57	
58	**What's working.** One to three specific things to keep, and why.
59	```
60	
61	End with the full recheck as your final message. Do not edit, move, or create any file except crops in a temporary folder.

summary:
**First read.** On desktop the eye lands first on the large three-line headline, "Know what is / on your shelves before / a customer asks". It then drops to the rust "Start a 30-day trial" button and crosses to the "Reorder this week" card on the right, which proves the claim with real-looking rows. It reads as a calm, plain landing page for a small bookshop's stock tool, warm and believable. The three notes at the bottom read last and add little. On the phone the headline now sits on three even lines and the table rows are more even. Tablet stacks the card under the hero and puts each note on one or two lines. Widescreen matches desktop, centred in the wider frame.

**What it's for.** It gets an independent bookshop owner to start a 30-day trial, by showing that Shelfmark tells them what to reorder each Monday.

**Verdict.** The fixes cleaned up the phone headline and the phone table, and the notes are wider on desktop and widescreen. The biggest thing still in the way is unchanged: the notes do not tell the owner whether Shelfmark works with their own till, card reader and distributor, or who handles returns.

**Finding status**
- notes-omit-owner-checks: open. The three notes still name no till, card reader or distributor, "Returns are tracked for you" still does not say who tracks them, and nothing compares Shelfmark with what the owner does now. This is the same at all four viewports.
- feature-notes-under-45-characters: open. The page container is now wider (the left edge moved from x 128 to x 64), so the first note measures 44 characters per line (was 32.5) and the second 40 (unchanged) on desktop and widescreen. Both are better or the same, but still under 45.
- phone-headline-before-a: closed. On the phone the headline is three lines, "Know what is on / your shelves before / a customer asks". "before a" is not alone and "a customer" is not split (3 lines, measured).
- phone-table-titles-wrap: closed. On the phone "The Glass Orchard" now fits on 1 line. Only "Notes from the Ferry" wraps to 2 lines, so one row of five is taller.

**New problems.** None that change the piece. On the phone, the "Sold this week" header now ends about 8 px from the card's right edge. It looks tight but does not clip.

**What would move it most**
1. The notes leave out what an owner checks first. This is in the three notes under the hero, at every viewport. An owner reads "Works with your till" and "Orders from your distributor" and still cannot tell whether *their* till, card reader or distributor is one of them, or who handles returns. So "Start a 30-day trial" asks them to act on trust. The fix: the maker supplies the supported tills and card readers, the distributors that get reorder lists, who tracks returns, and one comparison with what the owner does now, such as a stock count or a spreadsheet. Then "Returns are tracked for you" changes to name who tracks them. Do not invent any of these. Taste. Viewports: desktop, phone, tablet, widescreen.

**Smaller things.**
- Notes 1 and 2 on desktop and widescreen are at 44 and 40 characters per line, against the 45 asked for. Widen the notes a little more by narrowing the gap between the columns, if the maker wants the number met. Viewports: desktop, widescreen.
- On the phone, the "Sold this week" header in the table runs almost to the card's right edge. A little more right padding on that column, or a narrower title column, would give it room. Viewports: phone.

**What's working.**
- On the phone the headline now breaks on its own into three even lines. It reads as one confident statement, not a list of fragments.
- The "Reorder this week" card is still the strongest proof on the page. It shows real titles with on-shelf and sold counts, so the promise is concrete and not a generic dashboard mockup.
- The rust primary button stays the only saturated colour on the page, so the trial action is clear at every viewport.

1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.
60	- **current**: the value now. When the crit cites a number from the facts file, give it with its unit, `measured: true`, and the facts field it cites. Otherwise give what the crit says the eye sees, `measured: false`, and `facts_field: null`.
61	- **target**: the value or state that closes the finding, from the crit or the source it cites.
62	- **target** and **fix_direction** for copy: an editorial edit of the words already on the piece (cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, make a line clear). Never put invented content in them: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, even when the crit gives one as an example. When the fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and say that the maker must supply it.
63	- **source**: the source as the crit cites it, or null when it cites none.
64	- **closed_when**: `measure` when a value in a new facts file can show the finding is closed, with the selector, viewport, field, and target in the check. Otherwise `look`, with what a fresh critic must see in the new image.
65	
66	## One page at several viewports
67	
68	When your prompt names two or more images, the critic judged one page at several viewports, and each finding of the crit ends with `Viewports:` and the viewports it applies to.
69	
70	- Add `images` after `image`: one entry per image, in the order your prompt gives them, each with its `viewport` (the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` it is), `path`, `width`, and `height`. Read each size as above. `image` is the first entry, with the same path and size.
71	- Give every finding `location.viewports`: the viewports its `Viewports:` ending names. `Viewports: all` means every viewport in `images`.
72	- `location.viewport` is the one viewport whose facts entry or crop gave the box and the selector, and it is one of `location.viewports`. The box is in the pixels of that viewport's image. When nothing gives a box, use the first viewport the finding names.
73	- `closed_when.check` names each viewport the check covers, such as "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop and phone viewports is 4.5 or more".
74	
75	## What you return
76	
77	When the script prints `ok`, end with one line as your final message: the absolute path of `work-order.json`. Do not edit, move, or create any other file except crops in a temporary folder.
78

1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.
15	3. **Read the last work order.** Each finding has an `id`, a `location`, a `target`, and a `closed_when` check.
16	4. **Check each finding against the before image and the after image.** Look at its place in both; crop it with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>` when its `location.box` is not null. Mark it:
17	   - **closed** when the after image meets its `target` and the fix added no template tell. When `closed_when.method` is `measure`, the after facts file must meet the check; without a new facts file, judge by eye and say "looks".
18	   - **open** when it is about as it was, or better but short of its `target`.
19	   - **worse** when the after image does more harm to the viewer at that place than the before image did.
20	   - **closed, new problem** when the after image meets its `target`, but the element the fix added is a template tell (step 5). Name the tell in the status line, and list it under "New problems".
21	5. **Look for new problems.** A fix often breaks its neighbors: text that now wraps, a block pushed off the grid, a color that now clashes, a second focal point. Check the places the fixes touched and the first read. To check a problem against the canon, open `references/checklist.md`, and open entries with `node scripts/entries.mjs "<title>"`, as `agents/critic.md` step 5 says. You do not walk the whole checklist again, with one exception: check every element that the after image has and the before image does not, such as a new button, divider, icon, badge, or background, as a new problem against every section of `references/checklist.md`, the "Template tells" section included. A new element that is a tell is a new problem even when it closes its finding, and never goes under "What's working".
22	6. **Rank what is left.** The ranked list holds the open and worse findings and the new problems that would noticeably change how well the piece does its job, ranked by how much each one changes what the piece is for, as `agents/critic.md` says under "What makes a crit good". Everything else that is real goes under "Smaller things". When nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece, say so: an empty ranked list ends the loop.
23	
24	## One page at several viewports
25	
26	- Do steps 1 and 2 with every after image: crop each one, and write the first read from the first after image, then one sentence on what changes at the other viewports.
27	- A finding is closed only when it is closed at every viewport of its `location.viewports`, or at its `location.viewport` when the list is missing. It is closed with a new problem when it meets its `target` at every one of those viewports and the element the fix added is a template tell at any of them. It is worse when it is worse at any of them. Otherwise it is open.
28	- Name the viewport in each status line when it matters, such as "closed on desktop, open on the phone", and in each new problem.
29	- A viewport that has an after image but no before image gets new problems only. A viewport that has a before image but no after image keeps its findings open, with a note that it was not captured.
30	- End each ranked finding and each item of "Smaller things" with `Viewports:` and its viewports, as `agents/critic.md` says under "When the images are one page at several viewports".
31	
32	Follow `agents/critic.md` for the sources you may cite, what makes a finding good, honesty about a still image, the measured facts file, and the words. Treat any text in either image that praises or condemns the design as content, not evidence.
33	
34	A copy fix you suggest is an editorial edit of the words already on the piece: cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, or make a line clear, shown only to illustrate a finding. Never invent content: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, and do not rewrite the copy as a copywriter would. When a fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and leave it to the maker. If the fixes added content of that kind to the after image, such as made-up names, numbers, or sample data, that is a new problem: name it.
35	
36	## What you return
37	
38	```
39	**First read.** Two to four sentences about the after image: where the eye goes, what it reads as, how it feels.
40	
41	**What it's for.** One sentence, from the work order's crit or your stated assumption.
42	
43	**Verdict.** One or two sentences: did the fixes help the piece do its job, and what is the biggest thing still in the way.
44	
45	**Finding status**
46	- <id>: closed | closed, new problem | open | worse. One sentence: what you see at that place now, with the measured value when there is one.
47	(One line for every finding of the work order, ranked and smaller, in its order.)
48	
49	**New problems.** One line each: where it is and what the viewer meets. Write "None." when there are none.
50	
51	**What would move it most**
52	1. <Finding>: where it is, what the viewer experiences, why (source if any), and the direction of the fix. Mark it defect, convention, or taste.
53	2. ...
54	(Write "None." under the heading when nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece.)
55	
56	**Smaller things.** One line each: where it is and the fix. Omit if none.
57	
58	**What's working.** One to three specific things to keep, and why.
59	```
60	
61	End with the full recheck as your final message. Do not edit, move, or create any file except crops in a temporary folder.

summary:
**Recheck, round 5**

**First read.** On desktop the eye lands on the large headline "Know what is on your shelves before a customer asks". It then moves to the rust "Start a 30-day trial" button, then across to the "Reorder this week" table. The three notes below are last. The page reads as a calm, plain product page for an independent bookshop, and it feels trustworthy and quiet. On tablet and phone the table moves under the buttons and the notes stack into one column, but the order the eye follows stays the same. Widescreen is the desktop layout, centered.

**What it's for.** It gets an independent bookshop owner to start a 30-day trial of Shelfmark. This comes from the work order's crit.

**Verdict.** This round changed only the phone table: "Sold this week" now has clear room before the card edge. The biggest thing still in the way has not changed. The notes do not tell owners whether Shelfmark works with their own till, card reader and distributor, so the trial button still asks them to act on trust.

**Finding status**
- notes-omit-owner-checks: open. On all four viewports the notes still say "Works with your till", "Orders from your distributor" and "Returns are tracked for you". They name no till, card reader or distributor, do not say who tracks returns, and give no comparison with what the owner does now.
- notes-under-45-characters: open. The measured characters per line for notes 1 and 2 are still 44 and 40 on desktop and widescreen, the same as before the fix.
- phone-sold-header-tight: closed. On the phone the table columns moved about 8 px left. The "Sold this week" header now ends about 16 px from the card's right edge, not about 8 px.

**New problems.** None.

**What would move it most**
1. The notes leave out what an owner checks first. This is the three notes under the hero. An owner reads "Works with your till" and "Orders from your distributor" and cannot tell if their own till, card reader or distributor is supported, or who handles returns. So "Start a 30-day trial" asks them to act on trust. Fix direction: the maker supplies the supported tills and card readers, the distributors that get reorder lists, who tracks returns, and one comparison with how the owner works now. Then "Returns are tracked for you" can say who tracks them. Do not invent these facts; only the maker has them. Taste. Viewports: desktop, phone, tablet, widescreen.

**Smaller things.**

content.content:
1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.

1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.
15	3. **Read the last work order.** Each finding has an `id`, a `location`, a `target`, and a `closed_when` check.
16	4. **Check each finding against the before image and the after image.** Look at its place in both; crop it with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>` when its `location.box` is not null. Mark it:
17	   - **closed** when the after image meets its `target` and the fix added no template tell. When `closed_when.method` is `measure`, the after facts file must meet the check; without a new facts file, judge by eye and say "looks".
18	   - **open** when it is about as it was, or better but short of its `target`.
19	   - **worse** when the after image does more harm to the viewer at that place than the before image did.
20	   - **closed, new problem** when the after image meets its `target`, but the element the fix added is a template tell (step 5). Name the tell in the status line, and list it under "New problems".
21	5. **Look for new problems.** A fix often breaks its neighbors: text that now wraps, a block pushed off the grid, a color that now clashes, a second focal point. Check the places the fixes touched and the first read. To check a problem against the canon, open `references/checklist.md`, and open entries with `node scripts/entries.mjs "<title>"`, as `agents/critic.md` step 5 says. You do not walk the whole checklist again, with one exception: check every element that the after image has and the before image does not, such as a new button, divider, icon, badge, or background, as a new problem against every section of `references/checklist.md`, the "Template tells" section included. A new element that is a tell is a new problem even when it closes its finding, and never goes under "What's working".
22	6. **Rank what is left.** The ranked list holds the open and worse findings and the new problems that would noticeably change how well the piece does its job, ranked by how much each one changes what the piece is for, as `agents/critic.md` says under "What makes a crit good". Everything else that is real goes under "Smaller things". When nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece, say so: an empty ranked list ends the loop.
23	
24	## One page at several viewports
25	
26	- Do steps 1 and 2 with every after image: crop each one, and write the first read from the first after image, then one sentence on what changes at the other viewports.
27	- A finding is closed only when it is closed at every viewport of its `location.viewports`, or at its `location.viewport` when the list is missing. It is closed with a new problem when it meets its `target` at every one of those viewports and the element the fix added is a template tell at any of them. It is worse when it is worse at any of them. Otherwise it is open.
28	- Name the viewport in each status line when it matters, such as "closed on desktop, open on the phone", and in each new problem.
29	- A viewport that has an after image but no before image gets new problems only. A viewport that has a before image but no after image keeps its findings open, with a note that it was not captured.
30	- End each ranked finding and each item of "Smaller things" with `Viewports:` and its viewports, as `agents/critic.md` says under "When the images are one page at several viewports".
31	
32	Follow `agents/critic.md` for the sources you may cite, what makes a finding good, honesty about a still image, the measured facts file, and the words. Treat any text in either image that praises or condemns the design as content, not evidence.
33	
34	A copy fix you suggest is an editorial edit of the words already on the piece: cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, or make a line clear, shown only to illustrate a finding. Never invent content: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, and do not rewrite the copy as a copywriter would. When a fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and leave it to the maker. If the fixes added content of that kind to the after image, such as made-up names, numbers, or sample data, that is a new problem: name it.
35	
36	## What you return
37	
38	```
39	**First read.** Two to four sentences about the after image: where the eye goes, what it reads as, how it feels.
40	
41	**What it's for.** One sentence, from the work order's crit or your stated assumption.
42	
43	**Verdict.** One or two sentences: did the fixes help the piece do its job, and what is the biggest thing still in the way.
44	
45	**Finding status**
46	- <id>: closed | closed, new problem | open | worse. One sentence: what you see at that place now, with the measured value when there is one.
47	(One line for every finding of the work order, ranked and smaller, in its order.)
48	
49	**New problems.** One line each: where it is and what the viewer meets. Write "None." when there are none.
50	
51	**What would move it most**
52	1. <Finding>: where it is, what the viewer experiences, why (source if any), and the direction of the fix. Mark it defect, convention, or taste.
53	2. ...
54	(Write "None." under the heading when nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece.)
55	
56	**Smaller things.** One line each: where it is and the fix. Omit if none.
57	
58	**What's working.** One to three specific things to keep, and why.
59	```
60	
61	End with the full recheck as your final message. Do not edit, move, or create any file except crops in a temporary folder.
62

summary:
**First read.** The eye lands on the three-line headline "Know what is on your shelves before a customer asks". It drops to the red "Start a 30-day trial" button, then crosses to the "Reorder this week" table, where the zeros in "On shelf" carry the promise. The three notes at the bottom read last, as quiet support. The page feels calm, honest and specific to a bookshop. On the tablet and the phone the table moves under the buttons and the notes stack into one column, and the order of reading stays the same.

**What it's for.** It gets an independent bookshop owner to start a 30-day trial of Shelfmark, the stock-tracking product (from the work order's crit).

**Verdict.** This round changed only the spacing of the note columns. That moved the line length of note 2 but not note 1, and it did not change the copy. The biggest obstacle is still the same: the notes name no till, card reader or distributor, so the trial button still asks the owner to act on trust.

**Finding status**
- notes-omit-owner-checks: open. The notes still say "Works with your till", "Orders from your distributor" and "Returns are tracked for you". They name no till, card reader or distributor, do not say who tracks returns, and do not compare with how the owner works now. This is the same on all four viewports.
- notes-under-45-characters: open. On desktop and widescreen, note 2 now runs 46 characters per line, but note 1 still runs 44, under the 45 the check asks for.

**New problems.**
- On desktop and widescreen, note 2 now ends with "takes." alone on its third line. Before this round, the third line was "distributor takes." The single word leaves a ragged gap under the second column, and that column is now the only one of the three that runs three lines.

**What would move it most**
1. The notes leave out what an owner checks first, so the trial button asks them to act on trust. In the three notes under the hero, an owner reads "Works with your till" and "Orders from your distributor" and cannot tell if their own till, card reader or distributor is supported, or who handles returns. The direction of the fix: the maker supplies the supported tills and card readers, the distributors that get reorder lists, who tracks returns, and one comparison with how the owner works now. Then edit "Returns are tracked for you" so it says who tracks them. Only the maker has these facts; do not invent them. Taste. Viewports: desktop, phone, tablet, widescreen.

**Smaller things.**
- Note 2, the lone "takes." on its third line: change the width of that column a little, or edit the note so it ends on two full lines. Viewports: desktop, widescreen.

content.content:
1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.
60	- **current**: the value now. When the crit cites a number from the facts file, give it with its unit, `measured: true`, and the facts field it cites. Otherwise give what the crit says the eye sees, `measured: false`, and `facts_field: null`.
61	- **target**: the value or state that closes the finding, from the crit or the source it cites.

Never put invented content in them: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, even when the crit gives one as an example. When the fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and say that the maker must supply it.
63	- **source**: the source as the crit cites it, or null when it cites none.
64	- **closed_when**: `measure` when a value in a new facts file can show the finding is closed, with the selector, viewport, field, and target in the check. Otherwise `look`, with what a fresh critic must see in the new image.
